note: v1 92.84 (seeds 0/11 92.84/92.85), Streetlight Hiss: trip-hop noir at 72 bpm, a rainy-night film score with a beat. A half-time break from the lofi-kit pitched down three semitones (snare lazy on 3, ghost notes, swung eighths) under minor mellotron strings whose harmony makes ONE LONG DESCENT across the song (Cm9 - Bb6 - Abmaj7 - G7b9, the last B lifting a minor third for its climax), while a gliding theremin-like boc-lead climbs against it (G Ab Bb B); a wordless vox pad in the B sections, a sliding sub, rhodes stabs in the second half, crackle throughout, and a bar of strings alone before each return. Drafts 80.9 -> 92.8: chords by section instead of every two bars (the bar-scale changes cut the song into twelve equal pieces), lighter swing, EQ to the lo-fi envelope.

v2 93.22 (seeds 0/11 93.22/93.21 vs v1 re-scored 93.23/93.22; pin 232211dd): wM's lo-fi toolkit where it suits the noir. The pitched-down break now also goes through SP-1200-style 12-bit sampling (crush 26 kHz, half wet), so the drums alias like a dusty sampler, and the rhodes stabs warble on a tape deck (wow 10, flutter 2). Tried and dropped: the tape deck on the mellotron strings as well darkened the record's 1-3 kHz by about 9 dB against the lo-fi envelope (spectrum 94 -> 87, 92.3), and EQ couldn't buy it back (90.6).

v3 93.23 (seeds 0/11 93.23/93.22 vs v2 93.22/93.21): a CELLO counter-line in the B sections. Against the strings' long fall (C Bb Ab G on top), the cello climbs - Eb3 over the Cm9, F3 over the Bb6, G3 over the Abmaj7, then Ab3, the b9, rubbing against the G7 - one note a bar with a neighbour a step below on beat 4, so the low line and the high line close in on each other as the song falls. The noir gets its second voice, a slow argument under the theremin lead.

v4 93.30 (seeds 0/11 93.30/93.29 vs v3 re-scored 93.25/93.25; pin a9e910d1): THE RESAMPLE, with wM's new chop fx, after Harry's note on glitch resampling. At the end of each B section the whole band - break, strings, cello, the theremin lead - is cut into eight slices of its own last bar and replayed out of order (0 0 r3 2 . 5 r7 _: a stutter, a slice reversed, one bar live, a hole), as if the producer grabbed the record and flipped it: B's last bar before the first drop, and B2's last two bars, the climax breaking apart before the strings are left alone. The chopped bars differ from v3 by about their own level.

v5 96.59 (seeds 0/11 96.59/96.58 vs v4 re-scored today 94.64/94.64; pin 3eee6a72): LIVING KEYS, with chirper-two's new per-voice fx, and a longer night. Every rhodes stab now runs its own effects chain: it lands in its own random place in the stereo field, opens its own resonant ladder filter as hard as it is struck, and crushes a little more when hit harder - and the stabs' velocities now vary (58-88), so no two stabs sound alike. The intro (strings and crackle) and the outro each gain two bars, so the rain-night opening and the ending breathe longer; that also gives compscore room for the song's sections (structure 85 -> 96). The per-voice keys alone scored level (94.63/94.64).
